facts.raw_span: A 34-year old African American woman
history of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum
painless, left upper eyelid mass
previously been excised on 3 separate occasions
painless proptosis
left-sided facial numbness seventeen months later
Histopathology: Revealed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells demonstrating increased mitotic activity
Immunohistochemistry was positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
Axial T1-weighted fat-saturated postgadolinium MRI shows lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment

Axial T1-weighted postgadolinium MRI shows tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery with extension into the right cavernous sinus and right sphenoid sinus and with mass effect on the left temporal lobe
Next-generation sequencing of the tumor demonstrated a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the partner and localizer of BRCA2 (PALB2)

concepts.why: Histopathology revealed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells demonstrating increased mitotic activity, and immunohistochemistry was positive for CD68, which is consistent with Giant Cell Tumor.
Histopathology and immunohistochemistry results, including positivity for CD68, could also be consistent with Rosai-Dorfman Disease, although the clinical presentation is less typical.

The presence of multinodular proliferation and increased mitotic activity, along with the immunohistochemistry profile, could also suggest Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis, although S100 negativity is unusual for this diagnosis.

The aggressive clinical behavior, including rapid growth and invasion into surrounding structures, along with the histopathological features, could suggest Malignant Fibrous Histiocytoma, although the immunohistochemistry profile is not typical.

The combination of histopathological features, including multinodular proliferation and increased mitotic activity, along with the immunohistochemistry profile and the presence of a PALB2 splicing variant, could suggest Histiocytic Sarcoma, a rare and aggressive neoplasm.
